# Evidence-led report template

[Русский](report.md) · [Confidence guide](confidence.en.md)

Copy and complete these fields. Collect and publish only necessary data with an appropriate basis. The synthetic course case requires no personal data.

## 1. Question and answer

Title, version, researcher and date. State one precise question. Give a 3–5 sentence answer distinguishing supported, contradicted and unknown elements. Keep material caveats beside the findings.

## 2. Scope

Subject, applicable jurisdiction, period, cutoff, included sources, exclusions and access basis. State what was not examined. For the course: “Original synthetic corpus only, cutoff 2025-05-18T23:59:59Z.”

## 3. Method

Queries, filters, joins and tools; relevant versions; original and working-file locations; preservation and cleaning decisions. Explain how another researcher can repeat the work.

## 4. Claim-by-claim findings

```text
Claim ID and exact wording:
Status: supported / contradicted / unsupported / not examined
Observations and evidence IDs (file + record / passage):
Reasoning from observation to finding:
Confidence and its basis:
Material alternative / counterargument:
New evidence that would change the finding:
```

## 5. Limitations and publication review

Describe incomplete coverage, uncertain authorship, shared source origins, map precision and unknown timezones. Separate source limitations from method limitations. Explain minimization, redaction and retention where relevant. Do not infer motive or wrongdoing without evidence.

## 6. Appendices

Journal, evidence inventory with access dates and provenance, hashes if computed, cleaning decision ledger, captioned maps/frames and licensing information. Check that every finding points to a specific passage and every shared asset may be redistributed.

Final check: can a reader reproduce the numbers and trace the conclusions? “The supplied ledger records 5m” is appropriately bounded; “the company only ever received 5m” is not.
